newsitem.title: UK: British water companies pledge better service.
newsitem.headline: British water companies pledge better service.

text.p: Britain's water companies, criticised by consumer watchdogs for failing to prevent water shortages and for paying high salaries to board members, on Wednesday pledged to improve their service.

The Water Services Association, which groups the nine biggest privatised water and sewerage companies of England and Wales, said it aimed to turn from an "engineering-driven to a customer-driven business."

The association pledged to "make sure our customers have the water they want when they want it", produce the best quality drinking water in the world, be the most environmentally conscious industry in Britain and provide water services at the lowest possible cost to the customer.
Other pledges included leading the world in water technologies and strengthenging commitment to local communities.
Consumer groups have savaged the privatised water companies for failing to stem water leaks, cutting supplies and paying what they call grossly inflated packages to executives.
The association acknowledged it had failed sometimes to get its services right and that it expected to be held to account for its pledges.
